rule: Shrink-only ratchet for the gwz_transport_candidate clippy debt (operator decision D-U, 2026-10-31). scripts/checks/check_candidate_clippy.py runs clippy over the prepared candidate tree and fails on any (lint, file, enclosing item, unit) key that is not listed or whose count rose; it reports keys that fell so the list can shrink (--update rewrites it, and refuses if anything grew). Never add or raise an entry: fix the diagnostic. Every entry's owner is the plan step that removes it (6.1, GwzTransportReleaseConvergencePlan) and its class says what kind of debt it is (style, dead-code, design, concurrency). Entries are grouped by shape, one per OS (macos, linux; dead code differs by platform) and the script compares with the running platform's shape unless --shape names another. No line numbers: the item is read from the source by indentation.
command: RUSTFLAGS='--cfg gwz_transport_candidate' CLIPPY_CONF_DIR=scripts/checks/filesystem_lints cargo +1.95.0 clippy --no-deps --all-targets --all-features --locked --keep-going --message-format=json --manifest-path <prepare.py tree>/Cargo.toml (no -D warnings: a denied lint in the library would stop the units that depend on it)

macos.description: The candidate on macOS, all targets. Generated on macOS aarch64, rustc/clippy 1.95.0, gwz-core 25039b78 with gwz-transport 0a25363. cargo's JSON does not say whether a message came from the library or its test build, so both are unit gwz_core:lib and a diagnostic in library code that the test build repeats counts twice (65 library + 124 library test + 1 in the transport_placement_guide target = 190).

linux.description: The candidate on Linux, all targets. Derived from the macos shape using the Linux run on WSL (rustc/clippy 1.95.0): dead code differs by platform, so SshdFixture::with_startups (src/git/endpoint/ssh_fixture.rs) is dead on Linux and not on macOS, while https_fixture.rs leaf_digest and the transport_placement_guide fetch_using_client needless_update appear on macOS only. Every other key and count is the same as the macos shape (189 diagnostics = 190 - 2 + 1).
